observation.visible_scene: A small rectangular home aquarium with pink cylindrical gravel substrate and fixed ornaments: a pale lion-dog statue at left, a red windmill in the center, a cat-shaped hide at right, a tall green plastic plant, a black corrugated intake tube at right, pink sponge filters at left, and a suspended clear glass goblet in the upper-middle. Several orange/pink fish are present: a large orange goldfish near the center, a smaller orange fish at upper-left, a pale pinkish fish mid-left, an orange fish at lower-left, and a small pale fish by the plant. A thin stream of bubbles rises continuously in the central/right water column. The tank frame, background desk and lamp remain in the same position throughout.
visible_changes: The large central orange goldfish drifts leftward over the segment, starting mid-tank facing left and ending near the left side close to the lion statue and the lower-left fish, with its tail fins flexing as it swims.
The lower-left orange fish shifts slightly downward and stays on the left side, oriented head-down/left.
The upper-left small orange fish moves within the upper-left region and is later seen near/inside the suspended glass goblet bowl.
The pale pinkish mid-left fish makes small positional changes around the goblet stem and windmill, remaining in the left-center area.
The small pale fish by the green plant stays roughly in place with minor orientation changes.
The rising bubble stream and all decorations/gravel remain in fixed positions (no translation or deformation).
outside_clip_unknowns: Where the fish were before the crop and where they go after it; whether any fish entered or left the goblet by design.
The cause of the bubble stream (aerator/filter operation not shown).
uncertain_details: Whether the orange fish appearing in the goblet is the same individual as the upper-left fish or a separate one.
Possible minor handheld camera shake versus true static framing; background evidence is insufficient to confirm.
Exact species/identity of the small pale fish.
